name: Bathysphere Networks Inc. — Lake Michigan Deep Survey, Sectors 7-12 [PARTIAL RELEASE]
author: Bathysphere Networks Inc., Survey Division — Redacted for External Distribution
description: A partially redacted Bathysphere Networks internal survey report on the Lake Michigan floor, covering geological and biological changes, with notable gaps where findings were not cleared for release.
body:
BATHYSPHERE NETWORKS INCORPORATED LAKE MICHIGAN DEEP SURVEY — SECTORS 7 THROUGH 12 Survey Period: 2213.03.01 — 2213.08.15 Document Status: PARTIAL RELEASE — Sections marked [REDACTED] have been withheld pending internal review Author: Survey Division, Chicago Station

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY This survey covered approximately 11,000 square kilometers of lake floor in the central and northern basin, from a depth of 80 meters to the maximum surveyed depth of 281 meters. The survey was commissioned to update the 2198 bathymetric baseline and to assess changes in sediment composition, biological density, and infrastructure integrity for the sub-lake cable networks operated by clients under confidentiality agreement.

Key findings: sediment composition has changed significantly in sectors 9 and 11 (detailed below). Biological density and diversity in all sectors substantially exceeds 2198 baseline. Infrastructure assessments are provided under separate cover to affected clients.

[REDACTED — SECTIONS 1.1 THROUGH 1.4: PRELIMINARY SURVEY FINDINGS, SECTORS 7-8]

SECTION 2: SEDIMENT COMPOSITION CHANGES, SECTORS 9 AND 11 The most significant geological finding of this survey is the emergence of what our geologists have classified provisionally as 'exogenic carbonate formations' in sectors 9 and 11. These formations were absent from the 2198 survey and represent a substantial structural change to the floor in the affected areas. The formations are columnar, ranging from 0.3 to 2.1 meters in height, with a calcium carbonate composition that is consistent with biological precipitation — that is, they were created by living organisms, not geological processes.

The biological source of the formations has not been identified. The carbonate composition does not match any known species of freshwater mollusk, coral analog, or bacterial mat. The formations are, however, organized in patterns that our survey lead described as 'spatially non-random' — there is regularity to their distribution that exceeds what random biological colonization would produce. Whether this regularity is the result of a single organism with a large spatial footprint, a colonial organism with coordinated behavior, or something else is outside the scope of this survey to determine.

The formations are growing. Comparison of early-survey and late-survey imaging shows measurable growth over the five-month survey period.

SECTION 3: BIOLOGICAL DENSITY AND DIVERSITY All sectors show increased biological density relative to 2198 baseline, which is consistent with the general trend of lake recovery from industrial pollution. Sectors 7, 8, and 10 show recovery patterns that match ecological models. Sectors 9 and 11 do not.

In sectors 9 and 11, biological density is approximately [REDACTED] times the predicted recovery baseline. Species diversity includes [REDACTED] species that are not present in any freshwater biological database maintained by GLMZ or by the Great Lakes Environmental Compact. Of these, [REDACTED] have been submitted for classification. Of those submitted, [REDACTED] remain unclassified as of the date of this report. The survey team's biologist noted that several of the unclassified organisms displayed behavioral responses to survey vehicle approach that suggested [REDACTED].

[REDACTED — SECTION 4: SECTOR 11, DEEP BASIN OBSERVATIONS, 240-281 METER RANGE]

SECTION 5: SURVEY OPERATIONS NOTES The survey was conducted without significant operational incident with the following exceptions, logged for completeness.

Vehicle BN-7 experienced navigation system malfunction in sector 11 on 2213.06.14. The malfunction lasted 4 hours and 17 minutes. During this period, the vehicle operated on manual override and completed its assigned transect. The navigation system resumed normal function on return to sector 10. Review of the navigation logs during the malfunction period showed consistent compass heading readings that did not correspond to the vehicle's actual position as determined by surface triangulation. The discrepancy averaged 23 degrees. This has not been explained to the satisfaction of our engineering team.

On three separate occasions in sector 9, survey vehicles recorded audio artifacts in the 15-40 Hz range that are not attributable to vehicle systems, geological activity, or identified biological sources. The recordings are available to clients upon request. One member of the survey team requested early rotation following the second audio artifact event. This request was granted. The survey team member has not provided a statement regarding their reasons.

SECTION 6: CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS The Lake Michigan floor is healthier, by most biological metrics, than it has been in at least 150 years. The recovery from industrial impact has exceeded modeled expectations in most sectors.

Sectors 9 and 11 are recommended for follow-up survey with an expanded team and dedicated biological sampling capability. The formations and biological anomalies in these sectors require further characterization before definitive conclusions can be drawn.

[REDACTED — SECTION 7: INTERNAL RECOMMENDATIONS, RESTRICTED CIRCULATION]

Distribution: External release version — approved for client circulation by General Counsel, 2213.11.02
